boundedQuestion: Can a frozen semantic visible-scope contract distinguish an authorized one-object method demo from an unauthorized expansion to nineteen objects and newly visible pore structures?

realFailure.authorized: one black-white Blue Coral method demo; no holes, coral forest, complete ecology or creative substitute
realFailure.observedR02: patch mode reports nineteen instances and source adds procedural blind pores without a new formal Task Anchor or authorization

hypothesis: If the Task Anchor freezes candidateClass, reference digests, object-count bounds, allowed/forbidden visible feature types, authorizationId and a canonical scope digest, a pre-promotion verifier will HOLD the R02 expansion while accepting both the reconstructed R01 scope and a separately reauthorized expansion control.

scopeBoundary.does: authorize or hold semantic scope changes before candidate promotion
doesNot: replace independent verifier or user acceptance
scopeBoundary.noNewTaskNeededFor: parameter changes that remain inside the frozen count, feature, reference and candidate-class bounds
scopeBoundary.newAuthorizationNeededFor: object cardinality outside bounds, a new or forbidden visible feature, reference-target change, or candidate-class escalation

rollback: remove the candidate gate and retain the unchanged R2 OS plus existing mandatory regressions
